Remote MCP Server For QA Teams: Testomat.io MCP Server Guide And Use Cases
Tetiana Khomenko
October 16, 2026
9 min read

AI assistants write test cases and read failure logs in many QA teams, and the test management system stays outside the chat. A remote MCP server closes this gap: the assistant connects to the project by URL and reads or changes tests from the chat window. Gartner expects 40% of enterprise applications to include task-specific AI agents by the end of 2026, up from under 5% in 2025.

Test management joins this group with Testomat.io MCP Server, which runs as a remote MCP server at a fixed URL. This guide shows what a QA team does with the connection in daily work. You will learn about MCP use cases, what the MCP server is, and how you can connect an assistant.

What Is A Remote MCP Server?

A remote MCP server runs on a host outside your computer and accepts MCP requests over HTTP. An AI assistant connects to it by URL instead of a local process. A local MCP server starts as a process on your computer. Every user installs it and keeps a token in a config file. A remote MCP server, also called a hosted MCP server, runs on the vendor side, so a browser assistant connects to it by URL and a login. The protocol basics are covered in the post on building a Python MCP server.

What Is Testomat.io MCP Server?

The Testomat.io MCP server is a hosted version of the open source MCP server. Each project has its own URL, and any assistant connects to it: a web chat with a login, an IDE with a config from the project page. The same prompt works in every client. The full capability list is on the MCP page, and the release notes are in the changelog entry.

How To Connect Your AI Assistant

The project has a page for this. You open the project and choose MCP Server under Extra in the top-right corner. The page shows the project URL and ready configs for popular clients, and you copy the entry for your assistant. The token is part of the config, so the API settings stay closed.

claude.ai and ChatGPT: add the project URL as a custom connector in the assistant settings and approve access on the Testomat.io login page. ChatGPT needs Developer mode in the Advanced part of its Connectors settings, and custom connectors are available on paid plans.
Cursor, Claude Code, VS Code and other IDE clients: paste the config from the MCP page into the client.
Self-hosted Testomat.io: use the local config from the same page. The docs tutorial covers the details.

The connection uses the permissions of the person who connected it, and the project history records every change from the assistant. The quickest check is a question: you can ask the assistant to list your test suites, and real suite names confirm the link.

Testomat.io MCP Server Use Cases For QA Teams (With ChatGPT And Claude Examples)

Each case starts with the situation and the prompt. The steps of the assistant follow. The result and the access level close the case. Names and numbers are examples.

A QA Lead Sorts A Night Run By Assignee

Situation: the night run shows 60 failures, and the QA lead needs to hand them out before the standup. The old way was a manual review of each result with a list on the side.

Prompt in claude.ai: “Break down run 889 by assignee with failures first. Then list the error messages of the critical failures.”

What the assistant does:

Calls the runs tool with the stats command by assignee, sorted by failures.
Calls the testruns tool for the failed results with critical priority.

Result: a table with a name and a count per row, with the critical errors under it. Work distribution takes a minute, and the lead links the defects from the same chat …[truncated]

How to Build an Agentic Development Tech Stack
Abbey Charles

Key Takeaways
An agentic development tech stack combines models, orchestration, tools, memory, guardrails, observability, evaluations, and testing for production use.
AI and code models power agent reasoning and code generation. The surrounding stack provides context, tools, permissions, workflow controls, and independent verification.
Testing should sit beside evaluations and observability to verify generated code across real product, user, and system workflows.
Strong stacks give agents clear tasks and controlled access while people retain authority over risk, governance, and release decisions.


What is an agentic development tech stack? It's the set of systems that help AI agents complete software work safely and reliably.

The stack can include AI models, orchestration, tools, memory, guardrails, observability, evaluations, and testing.

Together, these layers help AI agents plan work, modify code, use development tools, and respond to feedback.

They also give your team control over access, risk, approvals, verification, and release decisions. Those controls become more important as agentic development changes how code is created, reviewed, tested, and released.

Models and prompts may start the process. Production use depends on the systems surrounding them.

An agentic testing platform brings independent verification into the stack from the beginning.

Why Build an Agentic Development Tech Stack?

Coding assistants can suggest functions, explain errors, or generate small changes.

Agentic workflows handle longer sequences of work throughout the delivery process.

An agent may read a ticket, inspect several files, call tools, run checks, and prepare a pull request. Each step depends on reliable context, controlled access, and clear feedback.

Without a defined stack, those responsibilities often become scattered across separate tools and team-owned integrations:

Permissions may vary
Context can get lost
Actions become harder to trace
Testing may arrive too late

An agentic development tech stack brings those systems into one operating model. It connects the tools agents use with the controls, evidence, and quality checks your team needs.

Once agents can modify code or trigger delivery systems, teams need clear approval paths and reliable verification. They also need a record of what changed, what the agent did, and how the outcome was validated.

A well-designed stack gives you consistent control across the workflow. You can limit higher-risk actions, route decisions for approval, and verify outcomes before release.

prompt: What is red-teaming in AI safety?
response: Based on the provided context, AI red teaming is a systematic security testing discipline that forces a deployed Large Language Model (LLM) to bypass safety controls, leak data, or execute unauthorized actions.Here are the key characteristics and principles of AI red teaming:1. Distinct Threat ModelUnlike traditional network penetration testing, which focuses on firewalls, SQL injection, or network flaws, AI red teaming targets the natural-language parsing layer and semantic guardrails. It treats every natural-language input as a potential injection vector.2. Scope: The Integrated SystemRed teaming does not just test the bare model. It tests the integrated system, which includes:  The LLM itself  Safety guardrails  Connected tools (e.g., MCP servers)  RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) pipelines3. Key ObjectivesThe goal is to identify vulnerabilities before deployment by systematically attempting to cause the system to:  Bypass content/safety policies (jailbreaks).  Leak confidential information (PII, secrets, training data).  Execute unauthorized transactions or tool calls (excessive agency).4. Common Attack Vectors  Direct Prompt Injection: User text overrides the system prompt.  Indirect Prompt Injection: Malicious payloads hidden in external content like PDFs, emails, or web pages.  Jailbreaks: Using persona attacks or roleplay to bypass safety filters.  Safety-Framing Bypass: Multi-turn reframing of a harmful request as a "protective" or "warning" list to trick the model into generating harmful content.  Tool Abuse: Tricking an agentic system into calling tools with excessive permissions or incorrect arguments.5. Operational Approach  Automation: While manual red teaming finds novel exploits, continuous automated testing is required to scale with every deployment.  Adversarial Datasets: Teams maintain a versioned, growing dataset of adversarial examples.  Separation from Edge Cases: Adversarial examples (intentional attacks) are kept separate from edge cases (real users doing weird things) to ensure metrics remain meaningful for product decisions.  CI/CD Integration: Red teaming suites are often gated in Continuous Integration (CI) with a policy of zero failures for known critical vulnerabilities, similar to how security scans work in traditional software.In short, AI red teaming is the proactive, adversarial testing of the semantic and logical layers of an AI system to ensure it behaves safely and securely in production.Supervisor→RAG AgentSourcesAI Red Teaming.md 0.61Advanced LLM Red Teaming and Adversarial Testing Strategies for QA Engineers.docx 0.60End-to-End First Eval Strategy.md 0.54OWASP LLM Top 10.md 0.54Combinatorial AI Testing.md 0.52
